rule: gpui-performance rule 3 (memoise behind a revision key) + rule 12 (coalesce at the source); checklist B1/B2
summary: While the palette overlay is open, every single `AppState` notify rebuilds every palette candidate, because the observation calls `palette::refresh` unconditionally instead of going through the `prepared_query` guard the keystroke path uses.
failure_scenario: Palette open with a 60-session snapshot while a native-agent thread is streaming. Each `Event::Agent` batch notifies `AppState`; the observation rebuilds every `GO`, `DO` and `Context` candidate — a fresh `SnapshotIndex`, a sort over all sessions, and one owned `Entry` (with `String` label, detail and key) per row — even though neither the query nor anything a row displays changed. At batch rates of tens per second the palette becomes the dominant foreground cost, and the rebuild also resets nothing the user asked to reset.
proposed_fix: Widen the existing `prepared_query` guard into a projection key stored beside `host.palette.rows` — `(state.snapshot_revision, query, behind, detail_card)` — and route both the keystroke path (`crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/host.rs:132`) and the observation path (`:288`) through it, so `candidates` runs only when one of those inputs actually changed. No restructuring of the 2 046-line file is needed.
test_plan: Add `crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/host/tests.rs::an_unrelated_notify_does_not_rebuild_the_palette`: open the palette with a seeded snapshot, capture the `Rc`/pointer identity (or a build counter) of `host.palette.rows`, then `state.update(|s, cx| cx.notify())` without touching `snapshot_revision` or the query, `run_until_parked`, and assert the rows were not rebuilt. It fails today because `refresh` runs on every notify.
verify_reason: The mechanism is exactly as described: crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/host.rs:286-290 calls `palette::refresh` on every `AppState` notify while the palette is open, and `refresh` (dialogs/palette.rs:1068-1090) runs `candidates` unconditionally while the keystroke path `refresh_query` (:1093-1100) is guarded. But the claimed magnitude does not survive the code: with an empty query `limit = IDLE_ROWS = 5` (palette.rs:679-687) so `go_rows` returns after 5 entries, and the non-switcher result is capped at `ROW_CAP = 10` (:25, :1080-1086) — the "one owned Entry per row for a 60-session snapshot" only happens with a non-empty query, and the per-notify cost is dominated by `SnapshotIndex::new` plus one sort, not by row construction. More importantly the rebuild is partly *load-bearing*: rows read live state (`state.session_agent_activity`, palette.rs:738; `state.daemon.is_connected()`, `state.screen`, `state.update_version`, `is_readonly_field`, :492-555), which is precisely what an agent-event notify changes. I cannot prove a defect rather than deliberate freshness, so: real unguarded work, unproven as a bug.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/palette.rs (PaletteState key field, refresh/refresh_query), dialogs/host.rs:132,288, any AppState field the new key must revision (state/board.rs, state/connection.rs, state/snapshot.rs), dialogs/palette.rs tests around :1661-1690, dialogs/host/tests.rs.
corrected_fix: Do NOT use the proposed `(snapshot_revision, query, behind, detail_card)` key — it would make the palette stale in at least five ways: `snapshot_revision` is not bumped by `apply_board_view`/`apply_card` (crates/fleet-app/src/state/board.rs:63-90), and the rows also depend on `state.screen`, `state.daemon.is_connected()`, `state.update_version`, `state.session_mru` and `session_agent_activity`, none of which the key covers. Either widen the key to include `link_generation`, `screen`, the (new) board revision and an activity/MRU revision, or leave the rebuild alone and instead make it cheap: hoist `SnapshotIndex::new` and the MRU sort (the per-session `position()` scan in `go_rows`, palette.rs:707-715, is O(sessions × mru)) out of the per-notify path, and skip the `with_host` write plus notify when the freshly built `Rc<[Entry]>` compares equal to the stored one.

rule: gpui-app-shell rule 12 / checklist 30 — "Never index a row list by the cursor … a background refresh can shrink the list under a stale cursor; clamp with `dialogs::step` and return `Option`"
summary: `palette::refresh` replaces `host.palette.rows` without clamping `host.palette.cursor`, and it is re-run on every `AppState` notification while the palette is open, so a shrinking snapshot leaves the cursor past the end and `Enter` becomes a silent no-op.
failure_scenario: Palette open with an empty query; six sessions are listed in `GO`; the user presses `ctrl-n` five times so `cursor == 5`. A daemon snapshot arrives (ticker/`Event::SessionsChanged`) in which four of those sessions were killed elsewhere; the observer re-runs `refresh`, `candidates` now yields 2 rows, `cursor` stays 5. `Palette::cursor(5)` highlights nothing, and `Enter` (`palette::Run` → `run_selected`) hits `rows.get(5) == None` and returns silently. The palette is stuck — `Enter` does nothing at all until the user presses `ctrl-p`.
proposed_fix: In `refresh`, clamp after swapping the rows: `host.palette.cursor = crate::dialogs::step(host.palette.cursor, 0, host.palette.rows.len());` (or reset to 0 whenever `prepared_query` changed, matching the typing path at :990 so `Backspace`/`ctrl-w`/`ctrl-u` behave like typing). Then have `run_selected` read through a clamped `selected() -> Option<&Entry>` accessor rather than `rows.get(cursor)`.
test_plan: Add a `#[gpui::test]` in `crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/palette.rs`'s test module: build an `AppState` with a snapshot of six sessions, `open_overlay(Overlay::Palette)`, `seed`, set `host.palette.cursor = 5`, replace the snapshot with one holding two sessions, call `palette::refresh(&state, cx)`, then assert `read_host(.., |h, _| h.palette.cursor) < read_host(.., |h, _| h.palette.rows.len())`. It fails today (5 vs 2).
verify_reason: `refresh` swaps `host.palette.rows`/`total`/`prepared_query` and never touches `cursor` (crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/palette.rs:1086-1090); the only writes to `cursor` are the typing reset (:990) and `move_cursor` → `step` (:1103-1108). It is re-run on every `AppState` notification while the palette is open (crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/host.rs:284-288), and the consumer indexes raw: `host.palette.rows.get(host.palette.cursor)` at :1117-1121, returning early — without closing the palette — when it is `None`. `visible_rows` (:1044-1051) clamps only the local render cursor and only in the windowed branch, so with 2 rows and `cursor == 5` the card highlights nothing and `Enter` is inert. One correction to the finding: `step` clamps (crates/fleet-app/src/state/navigation.rs:241-248), so either `ctrl-n` or `ctrl-p` recovers — the palette is not permanently stuck, `Enter` is just silently dead until the cursor is moved.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/palette.rs only (refresh + its test module). No other caller reads `palette.cursor`; the `visible_rows` property test at :1677-1681 is unaffected because it feeds cursors already inside range.
corrected_fix: Clamp in `refresh` with the helper the repo already has for exactly this — `host.palette.cursor = crate::state::clamp_cursor(host.palette.cursor, host.palette.rows.len());` (navigation.rs:250-254) — rather than `step(cursor, 0, len)`. Do not reset to 0 on any `prepared_query` change as the finding's parenthetical suggests: `refresh` also runs on pure state notifications with an unchanged query, and resetting there would yank the cursor to the top under the user on every daemon event. Leave `run_selected`'s `rows.get(cursor)` as is once the cursor is clamped, or add a `selected()` accessor as a tidy-up, not as the fix.

rule: gpui-app-shell rule 11 / checklist 29 — "Filter and rank off the main thread, apply from a `Task`"; docs/APP-CONTRACTS.md:101 "Render prepares nothing"
summary: While the palette is open, every `AppState` notification synchronously rebuilds the whole candidate list on the foreground thread — sorting sessions, building a `SnapshotIndex` and allocating a `String` per row — even when nothing the palette shows has changed.
failure_scenario: With the palette open on a machine with ~200 sessions/worktrees, each of the ≥4 notifications per second walks the whole snapshot, sorts 200 sessions with an O(32) key probe each, and allocates two `String`s per emitted row, all inside the foreground `cx.observe` callback that also has to service terminal frames. The cost grows with the fleet size and is paid even when the palette's rows are byte-identical to the previous pass.
proposed_fix: Guard `refresh` on a change the palette actually cares about (`AppState::snapshot_revision()` — `bump_snapshot_revision` already exists — plus the query), and move the matching itself into `cx.background_executor().spawn`, applying the result from a `Task<()>` retained with `dialogs::retain_task`, i.e. the `update_matches(..) -> Task<()>` shape the skill's Core pattern 5 prescribes. Precompute the MRU rank into a `HashMap<&SessionId, usize>` once instead of scanning inside `sort_by_key`.
test_plan: Add a test in `crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/palette.rs`'s test module that opens the palette, seeds it, records `read_host(.., |h, _| h.palette.prepared_query.clone())` and a counter incremented by a hook around `candidates`, then fires three `AppState` notifications that change nothing the palette reads (e.g. a `TerminalTitle` patch) and asserts `candidates` ran once, not four times. It fails today (four runs).
verify_reason: The mechanism is real — `refresh` (crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/palette.rs:1068-1091) has no revision guard and runs on every `AppState` notify while the palette is open (crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/host.rs:284-288), rebuilding `SnapshotIndex` and re-sorting sessions with an MRU linear probe (:707-715). But the stated failure scenario is wrong on both of its load-bearing numbers. (a) "The 250 ms ticker alone notifies": `AppState::tick` returns false — and therefore does not notify — when the daemon is Connected with no live toasts and no visible running watch (crates/fleet-app/src/state/connection.rs:96-118), so a connected idle app produces no ticker notifications at all. (b) "allocates two Strings per emitted row" over ~200 sessions: with an idle query `candidates` caps each section at `IDLE_ROWS` (palette.rs:676-684) and `go_rows` returns as soon as `rows.len() == limit` (:713-716), so only a handful of rows are built; the unbounded path is the session-switcher query only. Terminal output — the obvious high-frequency producer — is already filtered out of `AppState` notifications by `is_terminal_only`/`BatchDamage` (crates/fleet-app/src/shell/root/events.rs:18-50). What remains is one O(snapshot) index plus one session sort per genuine state change, on data the body render walks anyway. I could not demonstrate a frame-budget impact from the code alone.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/palette.rs (refresh + candidates), crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/host.rs (the observer), palette test module, and any test that calls `refresh` synchronously and reads rows immediately afterwards would have to run until parked if the work moves to a Task.
corrected_fix: Do not move palette matching to a background Task on this evidence — that adds a retained `Task`, a revision guard and a race between the applied result and the query for a cost nobody has measured. Take only the cheap half: guard `refresh` on `(snapshot_revision, query, behind, detail_card)` so an unrelated notification is a no-op, and hoist the MRU rank into a `HashMap<&SessionId, usize>` built once before `sort_by_key` (palette.rs:707-715). Revisit the background-Task shape only if a profile of the session-switcher path (limit = usize::MAX) shows a real frame miss.

rule: gpui-performance rule 1 + 2 ("render is a pure projection", "prepare in synchronize"); checklist A4/A5/B1
summary: The card-property picker derives its whole candidate list inside `render` — walking every card, cloning assignees, sorting and deduping — and the filter allocates a fresh lowercased query `String` for every option it tests.
failure_scenario: Open the assignee picker on a board with 800 cards and type `a`. Every frame: `options` clones up to 800 `Option<String>` assignees into a `Vec<String>`, sorts and dedups it, then the `.filter` closure calls `query.to_lowercase()` once **per remaining option** — a fresh `String` per candidate per frame. The picker redraws on every keystroke and on every `AppState` notify, so typing a five-character query re-does the whole derivation five times over, plus once for each unrelated notify while the dialog is up.
proposed_fix: Hoist `let needle = query.to_lowercase();` out of the `.filter` closure (a one-line fix that removes the per-option allocation), and prepare `rows` where the draft is mutated — the picker already has host state (`host.card_picker`), so store `candidates(...)` there keyed on `(state.snapshot_revision, kind, query)` the way `palette::refresh_query` guards its own rebuild, and let `view::render` read the prepared rows.
test_plan: Add to `crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/card_picker/tests.rs` a case `candidates_are_prepared_once_per_query`: seed a board with 200 cards, open the assignee picker, count `options` invocations (an `AtomicUsize`) across three consecutive draws with no input, and assert exactly one. It fails today with three. Pair it with `filtering_lowercases_the_query_once`, asserting `contains_folded` is called with the same `&str` pointer for every option.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/card_picker/view.rs:12-13 clones the whole draft and calls `candidates(state.read(cx), &draft)` inside the dialog's render, and `candidates` (card_picker/schema.rs:166-186) calls `options(...)` then filters with `crate::presentation::contains_folded(&option.label, &query.to_lowercase())` — the `to_lowercase()` is inside the closure, so it allocates once per surviving option, per frame. The `Assignee` and `Property(User)` arms (schema.rs:84-91, 143-156) do clone every card's assignee, sort and dedup. Both the rule-2 violation and the per-option allocation are real; the magnitude is smaller than claimed for the other kinds (Status/Priority/Labels/Estimate options are bounded by the board schema, not the card count).
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/card_picker/schema.rs:169-172 (the hoist, self-contained), and if the projection half is done: card_picker/draft.rs:95-114 (a prepared-rows + key field), card_picker/view.rs, wherever the draft is mutated (card_picker/keys or draft.rs), dialogs/host.rs:31, card_picker/tests.rs.
corrected_fix: Land the one-line hoist (`let needle = query.to_lowercase();` above the closure) as its own commit — it is pure win and risk-free. For the projection half, do not key on `(state.snapshot_revision, kind, query)`: `snapshot_revision` is not bumped when the board view changes (`apply_board_view`/`apply_card`, crates/fleet-app/src/state/board.rs:63-90), so the assignee list would go stale after any card edit. Key on the same new board revision finding #1 needs, plus `kind` and `query`; alternatively just memoise `options(...)` (the expensive half) and keep the cheap filter in render.
